title: Account Management
text: Manage information system accounts, including establishing, activating, modifying, reviewing, disabling, and removing accounts. Authorize access, grant the least privileges necessary, review accounts for compliance at least annually (or more frequently), and disable/remove accounts when no longer needed (AC-2).

title: Access Enforcement
text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies (AC-3). Access decisions are enforced at the system and application level for all users, groups, roles, and processes.

title: Information Flow Enforcement
text: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on applicable policy, e.g., by least privilege, separation of duties, and boundary protection (AC-4).

title: Separation of Duties
text: Separate duties of individuals as necessary to prevent malevolent activity without collusion, define system access authorizations to support separation of duties, and document the separation of duties of individuals (AC-5).

title: Least Privilege
text: Employ the concept of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) necessary to accomplish assigned tasks in accordance with organizational missions and business functions, including privileged account restrictions and prohibiting the use of privileged accounts for non-privileged functions (AC-6).

title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
text: Enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a defined time period, automatically lock the account/node for a defined period, or delay the next logon prompt (AC-7).

title: System Use Notification
text: Provide and display system use notification before granting access, informing users of: the system is for authorized use, monitoring/recording of sessions, prohibited activities, and consent/dev/usage policies (AC-8).

title: Session Lock
text: Prevent further activity on systems after a defined period of inactivity, initiating a session lock (or other use session), and retain the lock until the user re-establishes access (AC-11).

title: Session Termination
text: Automatically terminate user sessions after defined conditions or trigger events, including from organization-defined circumstances such as user-initiated logouts or period of inactivity (AC-12).

title: Remote Access
text: Establish and document usage restrictions, configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed, authorizing remote access prior to use, and controlling remote access sessions (AC-17).

title: Use of External Systems
text: Establish terms and conditions for individuals and system components using external systems, including untrusted external systems, and exercise oversight for organization-authorized processing stored on such systems (AC-20).

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
text: Provide security and privacy literacy training to all personnel, including role-based content, covering the foundational concepts (threats, risks, responsibilities) and required behavior (AT-2), with detection of phishing and other cyberattacks.

title: Role-Based Training
text: Provide role-based security and privacy training to personnel with assigned security- and privacy-related roles and responsibilities, including privileged users, before authorizing access and thereafter in accordance with training frequencies (AT-3).

title: Event Logging
text: Develop and maintain event logging capability per a risk management strategy: identify system events requiring logging, ensure audit records are generated for the events, and integrate with continuous monitoring per an authorization decision (AU-2).

title: Content of Audit Records
text: Ensure audit records contain the information needed to establish what events occurred, when, by whom, and from which sources, and to generate reports (AU-3), protecting the confidentiality of the recorded info.

title: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
text: Review and analyze audit records to identify inappropriate or unusual activity and to report findings to appropriate personnel; the frequency depends on the criticality and sensitivity of the systems (AU-6).

title: Protection of Audit Information
text: Protect audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion, including by separating audit information from other system data and restricting management functions to privileged users (AU-9).

title: Audit Record Generation
text: Provide audit record generation capability for the event types the system is capable of auditing, allow privileged users to select which event types are compiled into audit records, and generate audit records for the required event types (AU-12).

title: Control Assessments
text: Assess controls for effectiveness annually (or per an organization-defined frequency), as defined in the risk management strategy; include information system connections, and protect the assessment process and results (CA-2).

title: Continuous Monitoring
text: Develop and implement a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and maintain ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats: establishing metrics and assessment frequencies, correlating findings, trend analyses, and updating the strategy accordingly (CA-7).

title: Penetration Testing
text: Conduct penetration testing of the system at least annually, or per an organization-defined frequency, using approved tools, quantitative and qualitative techniques, and consistent with organizational rules (CA-8), involving both insider and outsider threat perspectives.

title: Internal System Connections
text: Authorize internal connections of system components or separate systems, document the connection characteristics (interfaces, data exchanged, security requirements) for each, and review the connections annually (CA-9).

title: Baseline Configuration
text: Develop, document, and maintain a current, baseline configuration of the system and its constituent components, including the systems/infrastructure/software inventory and associated configuration settings (CM-2).

title: Configuration Change Control
text: Control and track changes to the system components (configuration change control), determining the types of changes, reviewing change requests, determining the impact of proposed changes on security and privacy, and appointing responsible parties (CM-3).

title: Configuration Settings
text: Establish and document configuration settings for the system components, implement configurations, and detect and correct unauthorized deviations (e.g., via automated mechanisms) per organization-defined configuration standards (CM-6).

title: Least Functionality
text: Configure the system to provide only essential capabilities, disable/discourage nonessential programs, functions, and services, and explicitly prohibit or restrict use of organization-defined functions, ports, protocols, and services (CM-7).

title: System Component Inventory
text: Develop, document, and maintain an inventory of system components that accurately reflects the current system, including hardware and software within the authorization boundary, updated per the continuous monitoring strategy (CM-8).

title: User-Installed Software
text: Establish policies governing the installation of software by users, enforce via automated mechanisms, and monitor policy compliance, defining the software authorized for installation (CM-11).

title: Contingency Plan
text: Develop a contingency plan for the system addressing essential missions and business functions, including requirements, roles, schedules, and testing, coordinating with external service providers, and reviewing the plan at least annually (CP-2).

title: System Backup
text: Conduct backups of user-level and system-level information (including system state information) contained in the system, protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the backup information, and test backups per organization-defined frequency (CP-9).

title: System Recovery and Reconstitution
text: Provide the capability to restore and reconstitute the system to a known, functioning state within defined time periods (recovery objectives) after a disruption, emergency, or failure (CP-10).

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
text: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users (or processes acting on behalf of users) so that a user is always authenticated to the system, including via multifactor authentication for privileged accounts and network access (IA-2).

title: Authenticator Management
text: Manage system authenticators (passwords, tokens, keys) per policy: establishing initial authenticator content, ensuring delivery/receipt of authenticators, changing default content, change/refresh authenticators, protecting them from unauthorized reuse and disclosure, and revoking them (IA-5).

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users)
text: Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users (or processes acting on behalf of users) before allowing them access to the system, and prevent the reuse of identifiers for these users, consistent with the level of assurance required (IA-8).

title: Identity Proofing
text: Require proof of identity during the registration of individuals or devices before granting access, validating binding of the claimed identity, consistent with risk level, and notify the registrants of the results (IA-12).

title: Incident Response Training
text: Provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities, including training that is role-based and conducted in line with plans (IR-2).

title: Incident Handling
text: Implement an incident handling capability for security incidents, including preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery; coordinate efforts with the incident response plan and internal/external entities, and report incidents to designated authorities (IR-4).

title: Incident Reporting
text: Require personnel to report suspected security incidents to the incident response capability within the required time period, providing the incident reporting information as defined (IR-6).

title: Incident Response Plan
text: Develop an incident response plan that provides the roles, responsibilities, and procedures for responding to incidents across the organization, covering training, testing, coordination, incident handling structure and reporting, and be reviewed and updated at least annually (IR-8).

title: Media Sanitization
text: Sanitize system media (both digital and non-digital) prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or reuse for training/testing, using approved methods and documenting the results (MP-6).

title: Physical Access Authorizations
text: Develop and keep current a list of personnel who are authorized to access the facility and system where the system resides, and issue authorization credentials (PE-2).

title: Physical Access Control
text: Enforce physical access authorizations at all physical access points with control mechanisms (e.g., locks, badges, guards), audit physical access, monitor and log access to areas containing the system, and escort visitors (PE-3).

title: Monitoring Physical Access
text: Monitor physical access to the facility and the system, including reviewing physical access logs every defined period and investigating/responding to suspected or detected security incidents (PE-6).

title: System Security and Privacy Plans
text: Develop and maintain a security and privacy plan for the system that describes the system boundaries, environment of operation, security/privacy requirements implementation, and the connections with other systems, and update it when changes or assessments require (PL-2).

title: Information Security Program Plan
text: Develop and implement an organization-wide information security program plan that provides an overview of the requirements for the security program, and all resources, and is reviewed/updated at least annually (PM-1).

title: Risk Management Strategy
text: Establish and maintain a risk management strategy to guide and inform organizational risk decisions, including established thresholds for acceptable risk, and review/update it as needed (PM-9).

title: External Personnel Security
text: Establish personnel security requirements, such as position risk designations, background screening qualifications, and prohibited actions, for external personnel providing services to the organization (PS-7).

title: Risk Assessment
text: Conduct a risk assessment, either in full or in part, on an ongoing basis and with an updated risk model, threat source identification, variance identification, and an assessment of the likelihood, impact, and prioritization of risk to the system (RA-3).

title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
text: Determine information system vulnerabilities, including by scanning for vulnerabilities/hardware/software/web applications in accordance with organizationally defined frequency, using approved scanning tools, analyzing results via a risk management strategy, and reporting (RA-5).

title: Security and Privacy Engineering Principles
text: Apply system security engineering principles (such as a layered defense, indeterminacy minimization, and isolated functionality) in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the system (SA-8).

title: Developer Testing and Evaluation
text: Require developers to create and implement a security assessment plan, perform unit/integration/system/regression testing, evaluate penetration testing and verification of the security functions, and correct the identified weaknesses (SA-11).

title: Denial-of-Service Protection
text: Protect the system against or limit the effects of the types of denial-of-service events (e.g., resource exhaustion), employing features such as established rate limits boundaries (SC-5).

title: Boundary Protection
text: Monitor and control communications at the external boundaries of the system and at key internal boundaries within the system, through mechanisms such as boundary protection devices and network segregation (SC-7).

title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
text: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information, protecting it from unauthorized disclosure during transmission and detecting any unauthorized modification (SC-8).

title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
text: Establish and manage cryptographic keys using automated mechanisms, with supporting processes and procedures, per the cryptography policy (SC-12).

title: Cryptographic Protection
text: Implement the required cryptographic protections using validated (NIST FIPS-validated) cryptographic modules and algorithms governed by the cryptography policy (SC-13).

title: Protection of Information at Rest
text: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of information at rest, i.e., when not in active transit or in memory, implementing mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access, modification, or destruction (SC-28).

title: Process Isolation
text: Maintain a trusted execution environment for each executing process, by implementing separation of process execution domains, preventing unauthorized access to system resources, and isolating information (SC-39).

title: Flaw Remediation
text: Identify, report, and correct information system flaws and implement ongoing vulnerability remediation via automated mechanisms where possible, and test the software and firmware updates for effectiveness and for defects (SI-2).

title: Malicious Code Protection
text: Implement malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect, prevent, and eradicate malicious code, with automatic updates, central management, and non-privileged user policies (SI-3).

title: System Monitoring
text: Monitor the system and its constituent components to detect attacks, indicators of potential attacks, and unauthorized local/network/remote connections, using defined monitoring coverage and automated tools/alerts, and review them periodically (SI-4).

title: Security Alerts, Advisories, and Directives
text: Receive and generate organization-defined security alerts, advisories, and directives, disseminate them, and implement the appropriate actions, including coordinating internal responses (SI-5).

title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
text: Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to software, firmware, and information, and automatically take corrective actions or alert (SI-7).

title: Information Input Validation
text: Check the validity of information inputs to the system, such as comprehensiveness, validity, and tolerance ranges, using automation where feasible (SI-10).

title: Information Handling and Retention
text: Handle and retain information within the system and its output per applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards (SI-12).

title: Memory Protection
text: Implement security safeguards to protect system memory from unauthorized execution, protecting the system from malicious code (SI-16).
